candidates.original_title: Effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor agonist MK212 and 2A receptor antagonist MDL100907 on maternal behavior in postpartum female rats
candidates.description: Acute MK212 administration disrupts pup retrieval in postpartum female rats
candidates.citation_sentence: Chen et al. (2014) first reported that acute MK212 administration disrupts maternal responses in rats, especially for pup retrieval.
candidates.notes: Self-replication of Chen et al. (2014); authors explicitly state 'we replicated the acute disruptive effect of MK212 on pup retrieval' in Experiment 4 Results. Authors explicitly state 'we replicated the acute disruptive effect of MK212 on pup retrieval' in Experiment 4; this is a self-replication of their own prior work (Chen et al., 2014). The same acute MK212 disruption of pup retrieval is also confirmed in Experiment 1 results.

candidates.original_title: Effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor agonist MK212 and 2A receptor antagonist MDL100907 on maternal behavior in postpartum female rats
candidates.description: Acute systemic administration of the 5-HT2C receptor agonist MK212 disrupts active maternal behaviors in postpartum rats, particularly pup retrieval.
candidates.citation_sentence: In agreement with our previous report (Chen et al., 2014), acute MK212 injection severely disrupted various active components of maternal behavior.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 explicitly frames its finding as agreeing with Chen et al. (2014). [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor agonist MK212 and 2A receptor antagonist MDL100907 on maternal behavior in postpartum female rats
candidates.description: Acute administration of MK212 disrupts pup retrieval and other maternal behaviors in postpartum rats.
candidates.citation_sentence: This dose was chosen based on our previous work showing that acute injection of MK212 dose-dependently disrupts rat maternal performance with 2.0 mg/kg MK212 having the most disruption (Chen et al., 2014).
candidates.notes: Experiment 4 reports that it replicated the acute disruptive effect of MK212 on pup retrieval. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
